subject: Native function-shape borrow identity
claim: Decoded native shapes carry a separate Borrow-kind field. Function parameter/local parsing uses the version-aware reader and retains shape 37 payload identity without admitting WVB 1.39 to native lowering. The existing data/type boundary fixture passes as native code on Windows and Debian with identical WVB bytes.

limitations: Native WVB 1.39 admission, shape 29 Option-view storage, E1 instruction lowering, complete lifetime composition, owner retention/cleanup, exclusive borrowing, Take/Map and maintained consumer migration remain pending.

Shape 37 decoding supports only ordinary payload shapes already representable by the native reader. The matrix tests scalar, record, enum and callable identity; it is not general Vector, Sequence, fixed-array or variant-view execution evidence.

Version/truncation checks run on scalar and nominal boundary representatives; all 256 nominal entries receive identity checks. Every byte-valued payload tag is exercised against nominal zero (a record).

Initial fixture compilation rejected duplicate local names; corrected before final builds. Scalar runner attempts returned no diagnostic and are not passing evidence. The retained owner executes this fixture natively. PowerShell mapped its expected nonzero success code to a generic failure until LASTEXITCODE was inspected; both native products returned 42.
